1: # Feature: P1-E — Redis, S3 & SAP Infrastructure Adapters
2: 
3: Milestone: P1 — Contracts & Data Models
4: Milestone file: docs/agents-v0/milestones/p1-contracts-and-data-models.md
5: Story: P1-E
6: Surfaces: backend
7: Material: no
8: 
9: ## User story
10: 
11: As a platform administrator, I want foundational technical adapters for the Redis session and distributed lock store, S3-compatible object storage buckets with SHA-256 streaming, and the log-only SAP archival connector port, so that fail-closed session security, CSV artifact streaming, and post-endorsement ledger handoffs have resilient infrastructure bindings.
12: 
13: ## Acceptance criteria
14: 
15: ### AC-1 — store and retrieve Redis sessions, revocation blacklist entries, and distributed worker leases
16: Kind: happy
17: Given a configured Redis 7 (`sessionStore`) adapter port in `app/backend/`
18: When the `iam` session adapter stores, loads, updates (`effectiveViewAsRole` / `readOnlyOverlay`), or revokes a server-side session and checks the token/session revocation blacklist with configured TTLs, or the `execution` lock adapter acquires, renews, and releases a distributed worker/schedule lease key by owner token
19: Then the session claims (`userId`, `workspaceEmail`, `roles`, `effectiveViewAsRole`, `readOnlyOverlay`, `expiresAt`) and revocation entries are persisted and retrieved deterministically before TTL expiry, and distributed lease acquisition succeeds for the first holder, rejects concurrent conflicting lease holders (`false`), and releases or renews only when the caller's owner token matches
20: 
21: ### AC-2 — fail closed with SESSION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE when Redis session or revocation check is unreachable or times out
22: Kind: negative
23: Given a protected operation requiring server-side session lookup or token revocation verification against the Redis `sessionStore` adapter (`500 ms` connect / `1000 ms` operation timeout an
<truncated 10301 bytes>
aming (`_v2` / `_<epoch_ms>`) (`security-baseline.mdc` §5, §11; `docs/agents-v0/milestones/p1-contracts-and-data-models.md`).
83: - **Sensitive actions (for Design step-up / dual-control evaluation)**: Post-endorsement `SAP_REPORT_POSTING` archival copy to the immutable `archive` bucket and synchronous `LogOnlySapConnector` ledger handoff emission, which execute only under maker-checker approval and roll back atomically if either S3 copy or SAP log emission fails.
84: 
85: ## Regulations
86: 
87: - **BSP (Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas) Circular 982 / 1019 (IT Risk Management & Financial Audit Controls)**: Requires fail-closed session/revocation enforcement, cryptographic SHA-256 integrity verification (`checksum_sha256`) on all streamed financial CSVs and attachments, immutable 13-month archival storage of endorsed SAP commission reports (`_v2` / `_<epoch_ms>` collision preservation with zero overwrites), and atomic ledger handoff logging (`SAP_REPORT_POSTING_ARCHIVED`).
88: - **Philippines Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173) & GDPR**: Governs server-side session principal attributes (`workspaceEmail`, `userId`, `effectiveViewAsRole`) stored in Redis with bounded TTLs and log sanitization (`Encode.forJava()`) preventing credential, session ID, or raw financial row leakage in application logs.

102: - **Build (`/v0-build`, `implement-*`):** Verifies a green baseline, writes `docs/agents-v0/build/<feature>/plan.md` mapping every `AC-*` to a test, merges any approved `openapi.yaml` draft into the catalog, implements units via red-to-green TDD, and resolves the bound pack's native verify command with `.agents-v0/scripts/run-backend-verify.sh`. The script only prints. The caller executes the printed command.
103: - **Verify (`/v0-verify`, `quality-gate`, `vapt-review`, `pr-review`):** `test-engineer` runs the native stack verify command and checks AC test coverage (`quality-gate.md`); then `security-reviewer` (`vapt-checklist.md`) and `code-reviewer` (`code-review.md`) inspect `git diff <baseCommit>...HEAD`. Zero `Critical` findings sets `verifyPassed: true`.
104: - **Local Release (`/v0-local-release`, `local-release`) & Remote Release (`/v0-release`, `release-pr`):** `/v0-local-release` verifies `verifyPassed: true`, except a maintenance note with `tier: emergency` when `maintain` is approved and the note records a rollback plan and `Follow-up verify due` (full `/v0-verify` stays owed by that date). It re-runs the native verify command on a clean tree, and merges locally (`git merge --no-ff`) after explicit user approval. `/v0-release` prepares and opens a GitLab MR (`glab mr create`) for teams using remote merge requests.

6: 
7: # API design and event-driven behavior
8: 
9: Default envelopes: **`project-delivery-core.mdc`**. Implementation: `backend.mdc`.
10: 
11: ## REST / HTTP
12: 
13: - Resource URLs: `/api/v1/orders/{id}`; **201** create, **204** no-body success.
14: - **DTOs only** at the edge — never persistence entities from handlers.
15: - **Boundary validation:** validate request bodies, path params, and query params with the pack's schema/validator (`@Valid` / Bean Validation in Java, `[ApiController]` + DataAnnotations / FluentValidation in .NET, Pydantic v2 in Python, `binding` tags in Go, `ValidationPipe` / `class-validator` in Node) — no unsafe parsing.
16: - **OpenAPI:** keep code and the approved OpenAPI contract in sync (`@Operation`/`@ApiResponse` or pack equivalent where used).
17: 
18: ## Error responses — pick one per API surface
19: 
20: | Pattern | When |
21: |---------|------|
22: | **RFC 7807** (`application/problem+json`: `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`) | Public APIs, gateways, standard problem clients |
23: | **Custom envelope** (`success` / `error` — see `project-delivery-core.mdc`) | Internal platforms already standardized |
24: 
25: Do not mix shapes on the same base path without versioning. Document in OpenAPI.
26: 
27: ## Mutations and retries
28: 
29: - **Idempotency-Key** (or repo header) on **POST** and other non-idempotent creates/pays/cancels; persist key + outcome; replay same response within retention window.
30: - **PATCH:** document semantics (Merge Patch vs JSON Patch vs custom DTO) in OpenAPI; reject unknown fields if strict.
31: - **Optimistic concurrency:** **ETag** (or version) on GET; **`If-Match`** / version on writes; **412** / **409** per project convention.
32: 
33: ## Pagination
34: 
35: - Match existing contract: offset (`page`, `limit`) **or** cursor-based for large datasets.
36: - Cursor pagination: document `next_cursor`, stable ordering, opaque cursor rules.
37: 
38: ## Payload identifiers
39: 
40: Include **correlation** and **request** IDs in error payloads when the stack supports them.
41: 
42: ## Events and messaging
43: 
44: - **Idempotent consumers:** dedupe by `eventId` or natural key before side effects.
45: - **Retries:** bounded backoff; DLQ after max failures — **never** swallow silently.
46: - **Logging:** event id + hash or redacted summary — not full PII.
47: 
48: ### Schema and publishing
49: 
50: - Payload schema (Avro, JSON Schema) with **`eventVersion`**; schema registry + compatibility rules when org requires.
51: - **Evolution:** additive by default; breaking changes via new event type or versioned topic/subject.
52: - **Outbox vs direct publish:** prefer **transactional outbox** when domain write and event must commit together.
53: 
54: ### Event envelope
55: 
56: `eventId`, `eventType`, `eventVersion`, `timestamp`, `source`, `correlationId`, `data`, metadata (`idempotency_key`).
57: 
58: Example idempotent consumer deduplication (Java/Spring; apply the equivalent check in the bound pack):
59: ```java
60: @KafkaListener(topics = "orders")
61: public void process(OrderEvent event) {
62:   if (eventRepo.existsByEventId(event.getId())) {
63:     return;
64:   }
65:   orderService.process(event);
66:   eventRepo.saveProcessed(event.getId());
67: }
68: ```
69: 
70: ## Security at the boundary
71: 
72: - Parameterized queries only. Sort and filter fields come from an allowlist.
73: - Writes bind through a request DTO that rejects unknown properties.
74: - A user-supplied URL is fetched only when the host is on an allowlist. Redirects stay on that allowlist.
75: - No secrets in logs, responses, or client-facing exception messages.

7: - **Deciders:** mdurana

9: ## Context
10: 
11: Finance back-office desks transform heterogeneous financial input files (starting with the MVP Funding Cost Summary pipeline for five standard SAP commission reports: *Cashout Offline*, *Cashout Online*, *Cashin Offline*, *Cashin Online*, and *Real Time*) into strictly formatted enterprise CSV outputs under regulatory and audit scrutiny.
12: 
13: Key architectural forces from `user-requirements/Finance-Back-Office-Portal-Discovery-Requirements.md` and `docs/agents-v0/roadmap/finance-back-office-portal.md`:
14: 
15: 1. **Immediate MVP + Extensible Self-Service Platform:** Day-one delivery must support the five seeded Funding Cost Summary commission reports (`UPLOAD_ONLY`, files `< 50 MB`, `Asia/Manila` timezone, previous calendar month `YYYY-MM` period) while establishing reusable platform primitives (versioned JSON transformation recipes, managed reference lookup tables, universal maker-checker ticketing, and later a visual Report Builder and `S3_POLL` / `S3_OR_UPLOAD` scheduled ingestion behind `app.scheduler.enabled`).
16: 2. **Asynchronous Transformation with Runtime Freeze Guarantees:** Transformation jobs can run up to the `< 60 minutes` target (`docs/agents-v0/design/system/nfr-slo.md`) and must immediately return `HTTP 202 Accepted` while cycling through `JOB_QUEUED`, `RUNNING`, and terminal states (`SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`). Crucially, the platform must enforce an **immediate runtime execution freeze** that blocks approval/cutover of configuration tickets (`REPORT_DEFINITION_CHANGE`, `RECIPE_VERSION_PUBLISH`, `REFERENCE_TABLE_CHANGE`,
<truncated 11691 bytes>
l node capacity in `Later` milestones, the `execution` module (`jobWorker`) can be deployed as a separate worker container profile from the same compiled artifact without rewriting domain contracts.
79: - **Negative:**
80:   - Heavy CSV parsing inside the backend JVM could contend with interactive HTTP requests if unbounded; mitigated by sizing a dedicated, bounded worker thread pool (`executionTaskExecutor`), streaming CSV parsing (row-by-row rather than full DOM buffering), and enforcing strict `< 50 MB` / max-row limits.
81:   - Developers could bypass module boundaries via direct repository imports if unchecked; mitigated by mandatory ArchUnit structural fitness functions in CI.
82: - **Neutral:**
83:   - Asynchronous notifications (local SMTP email delivery) and transformation jobs use PostgreSQL-backed state tables (`notification_events`, `report_runs`) polled/dispatched by Spring `@Async` / `@Scheduled` workers rather than introducing an external message broker.

86: 
87: - `architecture-and-diagrams.mdc`: Single deployable modular monolith (`app/backend/`) with strict package boundaries (`execution`, `configuration`, `governance`, `iam`, `audit`) enforced by ArchUnit; single PostgreSQL database managed by Flyway; contract-first OpenAPI at `openapi/api-v1.yaml`.
88: - `security-baseline.mdc`: Google OIDC + Redis-backed `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax` session cookies failing closed on Redis unavailability (§1, §4); explicit `@PreAuthorize` on every controller endpoint with default-deny for unmapped routes and same-role BOLA/SoD checks (§2, F4, F8, F9); strict server-side CSV upload validation (§5); append-only 13-month security and mutation audit events (§12, F10).

9: ## User story
10: 
11: As a platform administrator, I want foundational technical adapters for the Redis session and distributed lock store, S3-compatible object storage buckets with SHA-256 streaming, and the log-only SAP archival connector port, so that fail-closed session security, CSV artifact streaming, and post-endorsement ledger handoffs have resilient infrastructure bindings.
12: 
13: ## Acceptance criteria
14: 
15: ### AC-1 — store and retrieve Redis sessions, revocation blacklist entries, and distributed worker leases
16: Kind: happy
17: Given a configured Redis 7 (`sessionStore`) adapter port in `app/backend/`
18: When the `iam` session adapter stores, loads, updates (`effectiveViewAsRole` / `readOnlyOverlay`), or revokes a server-side session and checks the token/session revocation blacklist with configured TTLs, or the `execution` lock adapter acquires, renews, and releases a distributed worker/schedule lease key by owner token
19: Then the session claims (`userId`, `workspaceEmail`, `roles`, `effectiveViewAsRole`, `readOnlyOverlay`, `expiresAt`) and revocation entries are persisted and retrieved deterministically before TTL expiry, and distributed lease acquisition succeeds for the first holder, rejects concurrent conflicting lease holders (`false`), and releases or renews only when the caller's owner token matches
20: 
21: ### AC-2 — fail closed with SESSION_STORE_UNAVAILABLE when Redis session or revocation check is unreachable or times out
22: Kind: negative
23: Given a protected operation requiring server-side session lookup or token revocation verification against the Redis `sessionStore` adapter (`500 ms` connect / `1000 ms` operation timeout an
<truncated 10301 bytes>
aming (`_v2` / `_<epoch_ms>`) (`security-baseline.mdc` §5, §11; `docs/agents-v0/milestones/p1-contracts-and-data-models.md`).
83: - **Sensitive actions (for Design step-up / dual-control evaluation)**: Post-endorsement `SAP_REPORT_POSTING` archival copy to the immutable `archive` bucket and synchronous `LogOnlySapConnector` ledger handoff emission, which execute only under maker-checker approval and roll back atomically if either S3 copy or SAP log emission fails.
84: 
85: ## Regulations
86: 
87: - **BSP (Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas) Circular 982 / 1019 (IT Risk Management & Financial Audit Controls)**: Requires fail-closed session/revocation enforcement, cryptographic SHA-256 integrity verification (`checksum_sha256`) on all streamed financial CSVs and attachments, immutable 13-month archival storage of endorsed SAP commission reports (`_v2` / `_<epoch_ms>` collision preservation with zero overwrites), and atomic ledger handoff logging (`SAP_REPORT_POSTING_ARCHIVED`).
88: - **Philippines Data Privacy Act of 2012 (RA 10173) & GDPR**: Governs server-side session principal attributes (`workspaceEmail`, `userId`, `effectiveViewAsRole`) stored in Redis with bounded TTLs and log sanitization (`Encode.forJava()`) preventing credential, session ID, or raw financial row leakage in application logs.
89: - **Internal GXI Enterprise Governance & Security Baseline (`security-baseline.mdc` §1, §2, §3, §5, §7, §11, §12 & VAPT F9, F10)**: Mandates fail-closed session store behavior (`HTTP 503` on cache outage), streaming file size enforcement (`< 50 MB`), path-traversal prevention on storage keys, outbound timeout and circuit-breaker resilience (`docs/agents-v0/network.md`), and ArchUnit bounded-context isolation.

2: 
3: - **Date:** 2026-10-29
4: - **Status:** Proposed
5: 
6: <!-- An Accepted ADR stays. A later decision writes the next file and sets this line to "Superseded by ADR <NN>". Do not edit Decision or Alternatives after Accepted. -->
7: - **Deciders:** mdurana
8: 
9: ## Context
10: 
11: Story `P1-E` (`p1-e-redis-s3-sap-infrastructure-adapters`) delivers the foundational technical infrastructure ports and adapters for Redis 7 (`sessionStore`), S3-compatible object storage (`objectStore`: `sources`, `artifacts`, and `archive` buckets), and the log-only SAP archival connector (`ledgerSink`) inside `app/backend/`. Governing requirements from `docs/agents-v0/requirements/p1-e-redis-s3-sap-infrastructure-adapters.md`, `docs/agents-v0/architecture.md`, `docs/agents-v0/network.md`, `docs/agents-v0/design/system/components/iam-access-control.md`, `docs/agents-v0/design/system/components/report-execution.md`, `docs/agents-v0/design/system/components/governance-ticketing.md`, and `ADR 0001` (`docs/agents-v0/adr/0001-modular-monolith-architecture.md`) establish six non-trivial engineering constraints:
12: 
13: 1. **Redis Session, Revocation Blacklist, and Distributed Worker Lease Semantics (`AC-1`):**
14:    - `com.example.app.iam` requires a server-side session and revocation store port (`SessionStorePort`) capable of storing, loading, updating (`effectiveViewAsRole` / `readOnlyOverlay`), and revoking sessions (`SessionClaims`: `sessionId`, `userId`, `workspaceEmail`, `roles`, `effectiveViewAsRole`, `readOnlyOverlay`, `expiresAt`) and checking/recording token or session revocation blacklist entries with deterministic TTL expiration.
15:    - `com.example.app.execution` requires a distributed worker and schedule lease port (`DistributedLockPort`) that acquires a lease ke
<truncated 13505 bytes>
`) before writing partial objects (`AC-3`, `AC-5`).
79:   - `RunArtifactStorageService`, `LogOnlySapConnector`, and `SapPostingApprovalArchiveService` resolve `archive` key collisions via `_v2` and `_<epoch_ms>` without overwriting existing objects, emit `Encode.forJava()`-sanitized `SAP_REPORT_POSTING_ARCHIVED` JSON events, and roll back atomically on S3 or connector failure (`AC-4`, `AC-5`).
80:   - `BoundedContextIsolationRules` and `LayerRulesTest` block cross-context access to `..adapter..`, `..repository..`, `..entity..`, and `..domain..` packages across all 5 bounded contexts (`AC-6`).
81: - **Negative:**
82:   - Executing the S3 archive copy inside the `SAP_REPORT_POSTING` approval transaction holds the row lock on the target `governance_tickets` row for the duration of the S3 `copyObject` call; acceptable because `copyObject` is a bucket-to-bucket copy of a single `< 50 MB` CSV and only one approver decides a given ticket at a time.
83: - **Neutral:**
84:   - Live HTTP controller endpoints (`/api/v1/auth/**`, `/api/v1/runs/**`, `/api/v1/tickets/**`) are wired onto these ports in Milestone `P2` and `P3` stories per `docs/agents-v0/requirements/p1-e-redis-s3-sap-infrastructure-adapters.md` (`## Out of scope`).
85: 
86: ## Compliance
87: 
88: - `architecture-and-diagrams.mdc`: Preserves modular monolith boundaries (`iam`, `configuration`, `execution`, `governance`, `audit`) enforced by ArchUnit; aligns with `docs/agents-v0/architecture.md`, `docs/agents-v0/network.md`, and component plans.
89: - `security-baseline.mdc`: Enforces fail-closed session/revocation store behavior (§1, §2, VAPT F9), server-side upload stream size cap (`<= 50 MB`) and path-traversal key rejection (§5, VAPT F3), `Encode.forJava()` log sanitization (§3, §12, VAPT F10), and ArchUnit bounded-context isolation (§2, VAPT F8).
90: - `project-delivery-core.mdc`: Uses `Pack: java` (`Java 21`, `Spring Boot 4.1.1`); Redis 7 (`sessionStore`) and S3 (`objectStore`) adapters are justified by `ADR 0001` and `docs/agents-v0/architecture.md`.
